question: The national highway network connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The national highway network that connects **Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata** is commonly referred to as the **Golden Quadrilateral**.
 
• It is a system of highways that spans a total length of **5,846 kilometers (3,633 miles) **and connects the four major metropolitan cities in **India.**
 
• **The Golden Quadrilateral was completed in 2012** and is considered a significant infrastructure achievement for India, as it has improved transportation and connectivity across the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Diamond Quadrilateral railway project is to develop high speed rail network across several metros of India.**
 
• This quadrilateral railway network connects major metro cities in India, i.e. **Delhi, Chennai, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Kolkata Hyderabad and Chennai.**
 
• This project is similar to **Golden Quadrilateral **which is** roadway project of India** which connects **four metros by express ways, the project falls under National Highways Development Project which has supported for better road transport in India.**
 
• In the same way to improve India’s rail infrastructure there is a need to implement **High speed trains/ Bullet trains.**
 
• **On 9th June 2014, The President of India Shree Pranab Mukherjee officially** announced that the government project led by **Prime Minister Sri Narendra Modi will launch a diamond quadrilateral project and fulfill the demand of high speed trains.**
